title: fix(console, grid): fewer requests per list navigation: one verdict probe per grouped list, preference writes only on change, poll backoff, palette keeps typed keys
body:
Part of #32627 — this delivers the four console call patterns; the two halves that need a new server capability are listed under "What remains" and stay on the card.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:分组列表每页只发两次权限解释(原来每组两次);列表偏好只在真的变了才写库;收件箱和审批在没有新内容时把轮询间隔从 60 秒逐步拉长到 3 分钟;按 ⌘K 后马上打的字不再丢。
- 为什么改:托管 HotCRM 上每次进列表都多发好几个请求,分组列表更多,轮询一直不停,⌘K 后前几个字会丢。
- 风险与回滚:风险在轮询退避(新消息最多晚 3 分钟出现,切回标签页立即刷新)和分组列表行数据改为全部分组到齐后才交给权限探测;回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts`(退避逻辑)、`ui/packages/app-shell/src/context/CommandPaletteProvider.tsx`(按键暂存)、`ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/objectGridGrouping.ts`(分组行何时交给权限探测)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/serverGroupedVerdictProbe-32627.test.tsx packages/app-shell/src/chrome/CommandPalette.typeahead-32627.test.tsx`,预期 2 个文件 6 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:卡上剩下的两半(一次列表只读一次权限、分组列表一次取数)要新的服务端能力,请决定是否另立 `domain:server` 卡。

## What changes

Measured first, against `origin/main` `6aa95dca5`, with in-process harnesses that render the real components and count every request (method below). Each item names the component that issues the call, how often, and why.

1. **Grouped list, `POST /api/v1/security/explain` per group.** `ObjectGrid` asks the record-grained write verdict (`useRecordCrudVerdicts`) for the rows in its `data`, one batched request per operation. A server-grouped grid fills `data` from each group's page as that page answers (`objectGridGrouping.ts`), so `data` grew once per group and every growth asked about the new rows: seven groups answering at different moments cost up to fourteen requests (the tenant reading). Now the grouped rows are handed over once every open group's page has answered; the rows on screen still draw per group as before. Grouped list: **2 requests** (one per operation, each carrying every row) instead of one pair per group.
2. **`PATCH sys_user_preference` per list navigation.** Measured: the per-navigation write is the **recents row** (`ui.recent`, `RecentItemsProvider` via `useTrackRouteAsRecent`), one per navigation to a list that is not already the most recent, and none when revisiting the head. That write carries a real change (a new head), and the recents store already compares against what it holds. The list-state writer (`ListPreferencesProvider`) did not: it wrote whenever a patch returned a new object, so a re-emitted sort, an unchanged column layout or "Clear all" over no filters each sent a write. It now compares the patched state's value with the previous one and with the value the store holds, and sends nothing when a patch changes no preference, including a change undone inside the debounce.
3. **Polling without backoff.** `sharedUserFeeds`' inbox and approvals feeds polled every 60 s for as long as the console stayed open, whatever they answered. Now a poll tick whose answer equals the value already on screen doubles the delay before the next tick, up to 3 minutes (the backgrounded cadence); the first changed answer, returning to the tab, and a push channel opening or closing restore the 60 s cadence. Every tick still reads the whole window, so an arrival is not dropped: it appears at the next tick. An unchanged answer keeps the published value, so consumers do not re-render for it. `inboxArrivals.ts` and `useRecordApprovals.ts` were read and left alone: the first is a pure diff over the feed's rows, the second has no cadence (mount and refresh only).
4. **⌘K drops the first keystrokes.** Opening the palette is a URL change (`?palette=1`), so its input mounts a render after the shortcut, and keys typed in between went to the page. `CommandPaletteProvider` now holds printable keys and Backspace from the moment an open is asked for (⌘K or the header search button) until the palette's input has focus, and `CommandPalette` applies them as the start of its query. The hold ends on the input's focus, on close, or after 2 s, so it never swallows keys the page should get.

### What remains on the card (not in this PR)

- **"At most one permission read per list navigation."** A flat list sends exactly two explain requests, `update` and `delete`, both batched over the page. `ExplainRequestSchema` (`packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts`) takes one `operation` per request, so two operations are two requests by contract. One request needs the explain contract to accept several operations: a spec and server change for `domain:server`.
- **"A grouped list fetches in one request."** Each open group pages its own rows (`useServerGroupRows`, ruling A on objectui#7189: rows inside a group are paged). The data door has no per-group window in one query (window functions are retired from the query vocabulary), so one request for N paged groups needs a new server capability. Not guessed here.
- Item 5 (dashboard chart latency) is not concluded on the card and is not touched.

## Tests

New pins, each with a CONTROL, and each made load-bearing by an ablation (below):

- `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/serverGroupedVerdictProbe-32627.test.tsx` — seven groups answering after different delays cost exactly one explain request per operation, each carrying all 14 rows. CONTROL: the same rows ungrouped cost the same two requests.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.userListState-12418.test.tsx`, new top-level `describe` "a list change writes the user's row only when it changes a preference (objectstack#32627)" — re-stated sort, unchanged column layout and "Clear all" over no filters send no write; a change undone before the debounce sends no write. CONTROL: a differing sort is one write, and undoing it after it landed is another.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/sharedInboxFeed.cadence-7249.test.tsx`, new top-level `describe` "a poll that finds nothing new asks less often" — an unchanged inbox is read at 0, 60, 180, 360 and 540 s; an arrival after the backoff is on screen at the next tick and restores the 60 s cadence; returning to the tab reads at once and restores it. CONTROL: an inbox that changes on every read keeps 60 s.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/chrome/CommandPalette.typeahead-32627.test.tsx` — ⌘K then "Acme" dispatched in one `act` (before the input exists): the query reads "Acme" and the page saw none of the keys; Backspace edits the held query. CONTROLS: with no open asked for, a key reaches the page untouched; once the input has focus, its keys are not held.

Pins of the old behaviour, updated on purpose:

- `sharedUserFeeds.pushChannel-27626.test.tsx` "with no channel, each feed reads at mount and then once per 60 s, never sooner": its ten-minute window answered the same empty value throughout, so it now reads 5 per feed (ticks at 60, 180, 360, 540 s), still never sooner than 60 s; a new CONTROL there keeps approvals at 11 when their answer changes on every read.
- `sharedInboxFeed.transient404.test.tsx` "resumes its normal cadence once revived": its revived feed now answers a different window each read, because the case tells a live feed from one on probes and is not about how a quiet inbox paces itself.
- `ObjectView.userListState-12418.test.tsx` gained `import '@objectstack/lint'` at module top, which `check:test-source-alias` asks of an edited file whose reach loads it lazily.

<details><summary>Ablation: every fix reverted to base, the pins go red, then restored</summary>

The five source files were restored from `6aa95dca5` (`git restore --source`, blob hash checked against the base blob and against the HEAD blob before running), the six pin files run, then `git checkout HEAD --` restored them and `git diff HEAD` read empty. Result with the fixes reverted: `Test Files 5 failed | 1 passed (6)`, `Tests 10 failed | 61 passed (71)`:

- grouped probe: 4 explain requests where the pin expects 2 (this fixture's stagger; the tenant measured 14);
- palette: `expected '' to be 'Acme'` (both cases);
- list state: the family's `save` called once where the pins expect none (both cases);
- polling: `expected 11 to be 5` (ten-minute unchanged window), `expected 7 to be 4` (arrival case and return-to-tab case), push-channel file `{ approvals: 11, inbox: 11 }` against `{ approvals: 5, inbox: 5 }` and, for its CONTROL, against `{ approvals: 11, inbox: 5 }` (that CONTROL's inbox half is itself a backoff pin).

Every other CONTROL stayed green with the fixes reverted.
</details>

<details><summary>Request counts per list navigation, before and after</summary>

Harnesses (in-process vitest, not committed): the real `ListView` and `ObjectGrid` over a counting data source and the explain double; the real `ObjectView` inside `UserStateAdaptersProvider` + `ListPreferencesProvider` with a counting list-state family; the real `ConsoleShell` / `ConnectedShell` over the fake preference framework, navigating `/apps/demo/OBJECT/view/all` across three lists and back.

| reading | before (`6aa95dca5`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| flat list, explain requests | 2 (`update`, `delete`, 14 ids each) | 2 (contract: one operation per request) |
| grouped list (7 groups, staggered), explain requests | 6 in the harness, 14 on the tenant | 2 |
| grouped list, data reads | 1 header query + 1 list window + 7 group pages | unchanged (needs a server capability) |
| list navigation, `ui.list.*` writes | 0 | 0 |
| list navigation, `ui.recent` writes | 1 per navigation to a list that is not the most recent, 0 on revisiting it | unchanged (a real change) |
| list-state patch that changes no preference | 1 write | 0 |
| inbox / approvals reads in 10 min, nothing changing | 11 / 11 | 5 / 5 |
| ⌘K then "Acme" in the opening window | query "" | query "Acme" |

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The tenant's per-navigation `PATCH` is the recents row and is a real change of that row. Whether recents should be written on every visit at all (or coalesced over a longer window, or kept per browser) is a product question, listed in the report for the seat; this PR does not change it.
- The ⌘K hold also starts on the header search button's open, the same `openCommandPalette` path; a `?palette=1` deep link holds nothing (no keystroke precedes it).
- The idle backoff ceiling is the existing backgrounded cadence (3 minutes), so a foreground tab never polls slower than a hidden one did; a quiet inbox's new message can take up to 3 minutes to reach the bell, and returning to the tab reads at once.
- Not measured in a browser: the counts above are from in-process harnesses over the real components, not from a running console against a tenant.
